issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch: the problem statement and UML require a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts the saloon name, but the provided solution implements a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()). The template repository does not include a SealSaloon class to implement. This mismatch can confuse students about the required constructor signature and prevents them from following the specification that a saloon must be constructed with a name.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a constructor SealSaloon(String name) in the SealSaloon class (in the template and solution). Either replace the no-arg constructor or add an overloaded constructor that stores the provided name in a private field. Update the template to include the SealSaloon class skeleton with the correct constructor signature so students implement the intended API.

issues.description: Missing 'name' attribute and corresponding getter: the problem statement explicitly says the constructor takes the saloon name and instructs adding getters for all private fields. The solution's SealSaloon class has no field to store the provided name and therefore no getter for it. This is a structural mismatch with the specification and the requirement to provide getters for private fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a private (likely final) String name field to SealSaloon, initialize it in the SealSaloon(String name) constructor, and provide a public getter getName(). Also update the template to mention/add the same field and getter so students implement the class with the expected attributes.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) specifies a SealSaloon constructor that takes a String parameter (SealSaloon(String)), but both the template usage (Main.java) and the provided solution implement and/or reference a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()). This mismatch in the constructor signature/API creates a conceptual mapping problem: students reading the problem expect to implement or call SealSaloon(String) while the starter code and reference solution use SealSaloon() (or only provide a no-arg constructor).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to expect a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) or add a SealSaloon(String name) constructor to the template and solution (initializing internal fields as needed). Preferably, implement SealSaloon(String name) in template and solution so it matches the UML and problem description (you may also keep a no-arg constructor delegating to the named constructor for convenience).
